A short paper tested 250 prompts on ChatGPT 4o using five different tones, from very polite to very rude. The results showed a small but consistent increase in accuracy as the prompts became less polite.

reels başlık: “Sam Altman on the two failure modes he fears most, and why both are catastrophic:” caption: “ Sam Altman on the two failure modes he fears most, and why both are catastrophic:

Asked whether he shares the worry about where AI is heading, Altman says he does:

"I do share the spirit of that worry. I really think there are two ways this technology can go very wrong."

He sets the specifics aside and looks at the two broad directions he thinks matter most.

Failure mode #1: Losing control to AI

This is the risk most people already know about.

"One which has gotten a lot of attention recently, is that there could be a loss of control to AI and that we build something that we don't have sufficiently aligned to human values."

His response is direct:

"And so we need to get safety right."

Why it's catastrophic: if we build systems that aren't aligned with human values, humans lose the ability to steer what comes next.

Failure mode #2: Concentrating power in too few hands

This is the risk that gets far less attention. Altman says it can come from the very effort to prevent the first one:

"If we do too much to restrict this technology in the name of safety, and we end up with a small number of companies or people or perhaps one country that have too much power over this, that also is a way that this can go horribly wrong."

Why it's catastrophic:

"People are shut out of the kind of power and benefits and control and agency over the future they should have."

So the two failure modes pull against each other. Too little attention to safety risks losing control of AI. Too much restriction in the name of safety risks handing it to a narrow few.

Overcorrecting against one danger can push you straight into the other.

@sama describes OpenAI's position as a deliberate balance between the two:

"So our goal here is to sort of be the pragmatic centrists between these paths, because we can see how tempting it is to err in one direction or the other." What are your thoughts on this?🤔💭” bugün 05.00

The IBM 7094 performed "Daisy Bell (Bicycle Built for Two" at Bell Labs, marking one of the earliest examples of computer-generated singing.

The moment even inspired a famous scene in Stanley Kubrick's 1968 film *2001: A Space Odyssey*, where the Al computer HAL 9000 sings the same song as it shuts down.
